calls.head: Wolf isn’t cursed against the Kraken
calls.body: Wolf has been shaky against the Kraken since 2023-24, well below his usual. It looks like a pattern, but across three seasons a goalie’s record against one team told us nothing about the next meeting. Expect the usual Wolf.
calls.call: If Wolf starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .906 than to his .855 against the Kraken.
calls.nums: 6 starts against Seattle: .855 save percentage · .906 against everyone else
calls.cite: Goalie starts since 2023-24 · 6 against Seattle, 3,405 shots against everyone else
calls.happened: D. Wolf stopped 21 of 27 shots (.778), against his usual .906 and his .855 against this team before tonight.

calls.head: The Flames should pile up the shots
calls.body: Seattle has been giving up shots all season, and the Flames rarely pass one up.
calls.call: The Flames take at least their usual 62.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5.
calls.nums: Calgary 5th for shot volume (62.5 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5) · Seattle 30th for shot suppression
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: Calgary took 73.3 shot attempts per 60 at 5-on-5 (adjusted for score and venue), against their usual 62.5.

calls.head: The Kraken can’t afford to cough it up
calls.body: The Flames turn stolen pucks into chances, and the Kraken are near the bottom of the league at avoiding breakdowns. A sloppy pass or two could cost the Kraken.
calls.call: The Flames get at least their usual 7.6% of their 5-on-5 chances right after winning the puck.
calls.nums: Calgary 8th for chances off turnovers (7.6% of their chances come right after winning the puck) · Seattle 26th for avoiding breakdowns
calls.cite: Style fingerprint · this season blended with last · 2 and 2 games this season
calls.happened: 23.0% of Calgary’s 5-on-5 chances came right after winning the puck, against their usual 7.6%.

SEA.head: We gave Seattle a 64% chance, and Seattle delivered.

CGY.head: We gave Calgary only a 36% chance, and it went the way we feared.

surprises.head: A rough night for D. Wolf
surprises.body: D. Wolf allowed 6 goals on shots worth 2.7 expected goals, 3.3 more than expected. Starting goalies had a night this rough about once every 50 starts over the last three seasons.

surprises.head: Seattle tried a different line
surprises.body: J. McCann, M. Beniers, M. Samoskevich played 13:21 together at 5-on-5, a trio that isn’t one of Seattle’s usual lines.

story.head: The Kraken roll past the Flames
paras: The Kraken had this one put away early. Berkly Catton opened the scoring early in the first. Mackie Samoskevich added two goals. It was 3-0 before the first period was half over. Five different Kraken scored.
The chances were closer than the score. The Kraken tried a line they hadn’t used before: Jared McCann, Matty Beniers and Samoskevich, and it had a hand in both of their goals.

items.text: The Flames haven’t won in three.
Whether the Kraken keep that line together at home against Vegas on Tuesday.
